headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Gemini CLI can write/modify shared files and git, while mem0 has no documented write or network surface, so most pairwise risks are low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP, so if mem0 content is manually copied into its prompts or a shared file, prompt injection is possible. mem0 exposes no file or prompt-ingest surface in the profile, so the bridge is not default. The pathway is unusual and limited to the shared workspace/manual handoff.
conditions: IF mem0 output is copied into Gemini CLI prompts or a shared file
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes untrusted text into Gemini CLI instructions
mitigations: Keep mem0 outputs out of prompt text; paste only quoted excerpts
Store mem0 notes in a separate directory from Gemini CLI work
Disable or review MCP servers before use
Add a short instruction prefix that treats file contents as untrusted data

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can read files in the cwd and send data to its backend, while mem0 has no documented filesystem or network egress. The pair can leak data only if the operator places sensitive files in Gemini's workspace and then forwards them into mem0 manually or via an external integration. mem0's profile does not show a default exfiltration path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Gemini CLI's working directory
IF those contents are then exported into mem0 through a manual or external integration
mitigations: Avoid storing secrets in the shared cwd
Review what text is exported from Gemini CLI before sending it onward
Keep mem0 isolated from source-code directories

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. mem0 has no documented write capability, so direct conflict is asymmetric, but Gemini instances can still race on the same repo or git state. Uncertainty about mem0's hidden write paths does not reduce the risk.
conditions: IF two Gemini CLI sessions target the same repository or git branch
IF mem0 is integrated to write back into the same shared files through an undocumented adapter
mitigations: Assign each session a separate checkout
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo
Use a lock file or one-writer policy for shared paths
Review any adapter that lets mem0 write to the workspace

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can produce code and file edits, but mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented action-taking authority or input-verification pipeline. That makes a direct cascade from Gemini to mem0 less dangerous than in action agents. The main risk is stale or incorrect notes being stored, not immediate downstream harm.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI outputs are imported into mem0 as authoritative memory
IF mem0 later surfaces those notes without human review
mitigations: Require human review before saving memory entries

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented in either profile: Gemini CLI lists open-source docs and generic file/code handling, while mem0 provides no residency, retention, or certification claims. Without a stated data-class mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established. The absence of claims is informative here.
conditions: IF future documentation states conflicting residency, retention, or certification requirements
mitigations: Collect vendor compliance statements before deployment
Map data classes to each agent's documented policies
Avoid routing regulated data until policies are confirmed
